subject: Competitive bake-off recap: OmniBar evaluation & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Christine Park <cpark@omnibar.ai>, Tom Evans <tevans@omnibar.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: OmniBar evaluation & next steps

Hi Christine / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Really helpful session. Below is a quick recap of what we heard from your side, the decision criteria you shared, and proposed next steps so the internal teams at OmniBar can run the bake-off. Please let us know if I missed anything.

Key pain points you raised
- Production token cost and predictable monthly spend (current spikes during peak inference hurt margins)
- Latency for interactive end-user flows (95th percentile target <= 250ms for short prompts)
- Model concurrency and capacity planning: need graceful degradation rather than failed requests during peak
- Auditability / traceability for responses tied to customer records

Goals for the bake-off
1) Validate top-line latency and cost per 1k tokens across representative workloads (see test plan attached)
2) Confirm rollout approach: can Redwood run in Dedicated mode in their VPC or do we need Private on-prem?
3) Evaluate quality delta vs your current vendor on 3 benchmark prompts (customer support, summarization, clinical triage)
4) Verify security posture (SOC2 evidence + KMS integration)

Decision criteria (your priorities)
- Security & compliance: must pass SOC2 + KMS for secrets
- Unit economics: < $X per 1k tokens target (TBD during pricing conversation)
- Latency SLOs at given concurrency (95p latency primary)
- Model quality: equal or better than VendorX on the three benchmark prompts

Open questions / dependencies
- Exact monthly committed throughput for Dedicated pricing (you mentioned 1–2M tokens/month; please confirm)
- Whether a vendor NDA/PO is required before Redwood can start dedicated testing inside your VPC
- Any PII/data residency constraints for the clinical triage samples

Proposed next steps
- Redwood to share a test plan (attached: redwood_test_plan.csv) and a short tradeoff matrix template for the bake-off (omnibar_tradeoff_matrix.xlsx) — ACTION: Marissa (today)
- OmniBar to confirm committed throughput range and preferred timeline for tests — ACTION: Christine (by 2027-05-24)
- Schedule a 60-min test kick-off (runbook + access) after NDAs are in place — ACTION: Tom to propose times

Attachments: redwood_test_plan.csv, omnibar_tradeoff_matrix.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0168

Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: OmniBar evaluation & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks accurate. A couple of quick clarifications:

- Monthly committed throughput: we're comfortable with a 1.5M tokens/month starting point for the Dedicated discussion.
- For the clinical triage samples, we can provide de-identified data; residency needs to stay in the US.
- We do need a vendor NDA before we exchange the de-identified clinical set (procurement requirement).

I'll loop in procurement (Sara) on the NDA. For the kick-off, Tom will propose times — earliest availability on our side is next Tue/Wed.

Attaching our requirements doc (omnibar_requirements_v2.pdf) — it includes more detail on latency windows and concurrency patterns.

Thanks,

- We'll scope two test runs: 1) low-latency interactive scenario (short prompts, concurrency up to 40) and 2) batch summarization run (longer context, measure cost/throughput).
- We'll provide a small evaluation Dedicated pool that can be placed in your VPC once NDA is signed; otherwise we can run a Private deploy if you need full on-prem.

Christine — we'll prepare the tradeoff matrix populated with Redwood numbers by EOD Wednesday (2027-05-26). I'll also attach the formal test plan and steps.

Subject: Test plan & quick security notes for OmniBar bake-off

Hi all —

Attached is the detailed test plan and a short checklist for security controls we'll need before placing any Dedicated capacity inside OmniBar's environment. Highlights:
- Test plan steps (see redwood_test_plan.csv): workload definitions, expected metrics, and logging hooks. We'll produce per-run CSVs with latency percentiles and token counts.
- Security checklist: SOC2 cert summary (we'll share the auditor's letter), KMS integration steps (we support customer-managed keys via AWS KMS), and audit log capture (export to your Splunk/S3)
- Data residency: we will ensure the evaluation Dedicated pool is in a US-region only; no data leaves region unless you request cross-region replication.

Proposed technical kickoff slots (PDT): Tue 2027-05-31 09:00 or Wed 2027-06-01 11:00 — Tom / Christine, please confirm.
